links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of LLM-generated and rewritten uveitis patient information
links.effect: ChatGPT mean FKGL 6.3 ± 1.2 vs Bard 10.5 ± 0.8; online uveitis information 11.0 ± 1.4; ChatGPT rewrote to 8.0 ± 1.0, Bard did not (11.1 ± 1.6).
links.quote: Online health information on uveitis had a mean grade level of 11.0 ± 1.4.

links.outcome: Reading level of patient-targeted uveitis materials versus a 6th grade target
links.effect: Online content mean grade level 11.0 ± 1.4; ChatGPT 6.3 ± 1.2 with grade-level prompt; Bard 10.5 ± 0.8; ChatGPT rewrite 8.0 ± 1.0; Bard rewrite 11.1 ± 1.6.
links.quote: The mean FKGL of responses to ChatGPT (6.3 ± 1.2) was significantly lower (P < 0.0001) than Bard 10.5 ± 0.8.

unlisted_practices: Prompting LLMs with an explicit target reading grade level to produce simpler patient education text

screen.reason: The study directly tests whether including specific reading-level constraints in prompts (prompt A specifying 6th grade level via FKGL vs generic prompt B for easy understanding) successfully alters the readability safeguard metrics of generated patient education materials.
